Fed expectations are holding fairly steady with the market pricing in roughly 33 basis points of rate hikes over the final two meetings of the year, with about 50/50 odds of a hike at the October 28th meeting, and an additional 35 basis points of increases expected in 2027. market_outlook: Adam's lean is cautiously mixed with a short-term bullish tilt driven purely by UN General Assembly diplomatic optimism and the possibility of a Middle East de-escalation, which would be the single biggest macro catalyst for lower oil, lower yields, and improved risk sentiment. The key catalyst to watch today and this week is any signal of diplomatic progress between the US and Iran at the UN General Assembly, as well as the Thursday Trump/Xi summit for potential tariff relief.
bull_case: The UN General Assembly running September 22-28 in New York brings together officials from Iran and multiple Middle Eastern countries, creating a rare opening for diplomatic progress. Even a small improvement in Middle East tensions could trigger an outsized drop in oil prices, which would cascade positively into lower yields, reduced inflation, better corporate margins, and improved consumer confidence. Trump reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday and said he would be open to meeting Iran's president, signaling a potential de-escalation. The Trump/Xi summit on Thursday could also deliver modest tariff reductions and a trade truce extension, providing an additional boost to sentiment.
bear_case: Nearly all weekend news flow was net negative — Houthis dramatically escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia, Ukraine launched its largest drone strike on Russia, and a wave of troubling AI headlines hit after Friday's close including a delayed Anthropic IPO, disappointing Anthropic 2027 ARR projections, OpenAI's massive cash burn, and Oracle data center debt issues. Geopolitical risks remain deeply entrenched with Iran tightening its grip on global energy supplies via Hormuz, aligned militias in Iraq, and the Houthis, while tanker shortages and surging motor oil prices signal real economic pain filtering through the system. The US-China trade truce extension was not reached over the weekend, and Washington is expected to hike aggregate tariff rates on Chinese imports back to pre-SCOTUS levels in coming weeks, maintaining a ceiling on any sustained risk rally.

The lack of specificity at the capital markets event is being read as a negative signal. Shares are underperforming in Europe this morning.

tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your morning game plan for Monday September 21st.

The macro setup is unusual this morning. Futures are rallying — S&P up about 49 points, Nasdaq up 329, Russell up 47 basis points — despite a weekend that was nearly wall-to-wall negative news. Asia closed broadly higher, Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points, and Treasury yields are down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve. The one thing holding this market up is diplomatic optimism around the United Nations General Assembly, which runs this week in New York. Trump said he'd be open to meeting Iran's president, who is expected to attend. He also reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. Markets are betting that even a small improvement in Middle East tensions could trigger a sharp drop in oil, and right now oil is the root cause of nearly every macro headache — elevated yields, inflation, margin pressure, weak consumer confidence. Brent is already sliding about 170 basis points this morning to around 102 dollars.

On the Fed and rates front, officials remain firmly hawkish. The market is pricing in about 33 basis points of hikes over the final two meetings of the year, with roughly 50/50 odds of a move at the October 28th meeting. Kansas City Fed President Schmid said Friday that inflation is running too hot even without oil, and Minneapolis Fed's Kashkari echoed that Sunday morning. Meanwhile Treasury is set to issue over one trillion dollars in T-bills over the next 12 months as Bessent leans on short-term debt to fund the government, pushing bills above 24 percent of marketable debt.

On the company side, Novo Nordisk is the standout negative this morning — shares are slumping in Europe after management failed to deliver granular financial targets at its analyst day, disappointing investors looking for clarity. Oracle remains under pressure after a Friday Financial Times report flagged stress in debt tied to its massive New Mexico data center project, with loan offloading efforts having hit a wall. This feeds into a broader AI infrastructure concern — Big Tech off-balance-sheet liabilities rose roughly 300 billion dollars in just the last 12 months, OpenAI is projecting negative free cash flow of about 280 billion dollars through 2030, and the Anthropic IPO has been delayed with underwhelming 2027 revenue projections leaking out. Despite all this, European data center pick-and-shovel stocks are outperforming this morning. Disney is a quiet positive — its parks business is outperforming peers by leaning on promotions and package deals while the rest of the industry deals with traffic headwinds.

The US-China angle is worth watching. Bessent called weekend trade talks very successful but no truce extension was reached — that truce doesn't expire until November 10th so it's not urgent yet. The bigger event is Thursday's Trump-Xi summit, where modest tariff reductions on roughly 30 billion dollars of goods and potential elimination of Chinese tariffs on American liquefied natural gas are on the table.

Directionally, the bull case rests entirely on Middle East diplomacy delivering even a marginal improvement this week. The bear case is that the weekend news flow was genuinely bad across geopolitics and AI, the rally feels thin, and structural energy supply constraints are not going away. Trade cautiously and keep your eye on any Iran-related headlines out of New York this week — that is the single biggest macro variable in play right now.
